title: check-platform-checklist's self-test D4 uses a strict `<`, so draining two more bad citations reds the gate for doing what #18104 asks — and the drain's end state reds it permanently
body:
Path: none | instrument (checklist gate self-test) | 北极星「仪器为车队服务」

`check-platform-checklist`'s own self-test **D4** asserts the `accept-set` rows are a strict minority of the `bad-citation` rows — so draining **two more** bad citations turns the gate red for doing exactly what #18104 asks, and the drain's terminal state makes it red forever.

Filed by the `domain:devx` execution PM seat (session `session_017ef78bLdybu3AffehKkhfk`) out of cut 3's `out_of_scope_findings` on **#18104** / PR #19232. ⛔ Not graded, no `domain:*` — that is triage's. **Expected landing point: `scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs` ⇒ `domain:devx` by SUBJECT.**

## The assertion, verbatim

`scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs:2248-2250`:

```js
t('D4 the `accept-set` rows are the minority and are named as a DIFFERENT card — ⛔ nothing here widens the shared core',
  SHARED_RESOLVER_RESIDUAL.filter((r) => r.verdict === 'accept-set').length
    < SHARED_RESOLVER_RESIDUAL.filter((r) => r.verdict === 'bad-citation').length);
```

⭐ The comparison is a **strict `<`**. That is the whole defect: it fails at *equality*, not only when `accept-set` exceeds `bad-citation`.

## ⚠️ The arithmetic, measured on PR #19232's head `76e8df900`

Ledger after cut 3: **18 rows = 10 `bad-citation` + 8 `accept-set`** (ceiling 18, rows == ceiling).

| next slice drains | D4 evaluates | verdict |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 row | `8 < 9` | ✅ green |
| **2 rows** | `8 < 8` | ⛔ **RED** |
| 3 rows | `8 < 7` | ⛔ RED |
| all 10 (the drain's goal) | `8 < 0` | ⛔ **permanently RED** |

⚠️ **Correction to the reading this was handed over with**: cut 3's report says the break comes at "3 or more". Measured against the real ledger it comes at **2** — the strict `<` fails on equality. A cut sized at two rows would look safe under the looser reading and would red the gate.

⇒ Reproducible today, cheaply: delete any 2 `bad-citation` rows from the ledger and run `node scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs --self-test`.

## ⭐ Why this is worth a card and not a note

The 8 `accept-set` rows **cannot leave** without a maintainer letter on **#18101**. So D4 now couples two cards that neither of them names:

- **#18104** cannot finish its drain without turning D4 red;
- **#18101**'s letter is the only thing that can remove the other side of the comparison.

⇒ A gate's self-test is quietly holding one card hostage to another's pending decision. Nobody reading either card can see that — it is visible only in the assertion.

## ⛔ What the repair must NOT be

⛔ **Do not delete D4, and ⛔ do not relax it to `<=`.** Its subject is real and worth keeping: it exists so the `accept-set` bucket cannot quietly become the main population, which is how «nothing here widens the shared core» is enforced. `<=` merely moves the cliff by one row and leaves the terminal state red.

## What the repair plausibly is (⛔ not prescribed)

The invariant D4 wants is about the *residual's* composition while a drain is in progress — not about a terminal state where `bad-citation` is legitimately zero because the work finished. Any repair should keep D4 able to catch the thing it was built for (an `accept-set` bucket growing into the main population) while letting a **completed** drain be green. ⛔ This card does not choose the spelling, and the reading that the drain's end state is legitimate is the load-bearing judgement — put it to whoever owns this gate.

⚠️ Whoever takes it: the gate's `--self-test` is 221 assertions and runs from source (no build), so reproduction is cheap; `node scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs` (census) is the other half.

Refs: #18104 (the drain) · #18101 (the letter that frees the `accept-set` rows) · PR #19232 (cut 3, the state above)
